speaker: Doctor
text: I see you are experiencing fatigue, abdominal pain, night sweats, weight loss, and enlarged supraclavicular lymph nodes; to begin my evaluation, have you recently noticed any fevers or changes in your skin? REQUEST TEST: Complete_Blood_Count, Comprehensive_Metabolic_Panel, LDH, and ESR.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Complete_Blood_Count: WBC: Elevated, Hemoglobin: Slightly Decreased, Platelets: Normal; Lactate_Dehydrogenase: Elevated; Comprehensive_Metabolic_Panel: NORMAL READINGS; ESR: NORMAL READINGS

speaker: Patient
text: I have been feeling very tired and have had worsening abdominal pain for about four weeks. I have also had drenching night sweats and lost about twelve pounds.

speaker: Patient
text: I noticed swelling in my neck over the last few days. It does not hurt, but it feels enlarged and fixed.

speaker: Patient
text: I also feel fullness in my abdomen and my clothes feel tighter. I do not have cough or recent travel.

speaker: Patient
text: I have smoked about one pack a day for many years, and I drink socially. The abdominal discomfort and fatigue have both been getting worse. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Tuberculosis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details; while your history of smoking and the doctor's suspicion of Tuberculosis are noted, I must independently evaluate this. Given the supraclavicular lymphadenopathy and systemic symptoms, have you experienced any cough, hemoptysis, or gastrointestinal bleeding like vomiting blood or black stools? REQUEST TEST: Chest_X-Ray, Abdominal_Ultrasound, and Sputum_Culture.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Chest_X-Ray: NORMAL READINGS; Abdominal_Ultrasound: Splenomegaly detected; Sputum_Culture: NORMAL READINGS

speaker: Doctor
text: The chest X-ray and sputum culture effectively rule out active Tuberculosis, so let's focus on the splenomegaly and lymph node findings. Given your "B symptoms" (fever, night sweats, weight loss) and smoking history, have you noticed any pain in your right upper abdomen, and do you have a family history of blood cancers? REQUEST TEST: Peripheral_Blood_Smear, Liver_Function_Tests, and Abdominal_CT_with_Contrast.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Peripheral_Blood_Smear: Lymphocytes with a high proliferative index; Liver_Function_Tests: NORMAL READINGS; Abdominal_CT_with_Contrast: Splenomegaly detected; Massively enlarged axillary, mediastinal, and cervical lymph nodes.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Lymphoma. The combination of B-symptoms (fever, night sweats, weight loss), significant lymphadenopathy (cervical, axillary, mediastinal), splenomegaly, and a peripheral blood smear showing lymphocytes with a high proliferative index is highly indicative of lymphoma.
